title: Who picks the number of orders
objective: NEVER-NEST-20261118-001's first direction, chosen by the coordinator: the never-nest rules hold two orders because they are told the number two (A101). Does any rule told no number settle at two from a line, or is the number always handed over, by a cap, a price, the start, or the arity of one move? Caps of d orders, prices on states and orders, conservative rules (fewest orders first; the corner rule) and rules that name only 'crosses nothing' (fresh crossings; no new crossing between crossed splits; seed and copy), from lines of 5 to 12 and from Q3 and the 3 x 3 x 3 grid. Serves G1 and G16; challenges A101.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; referee hand-off; report.
